SECTION IV
UNAVOIDABLE ADVERSE IMPACTS
The following is a summary of the unavoidable adverse environmental impacts of the CDBG program. Mitigation measures have been identified in Section III, Project Impacts and Mitigation Measures. The positive impacts of each project are also discussed in Section III.
Rehabilitation (Campus, Gardner, Mayfair, Northside, Olinder)
-- Short-term local increases in airborne particulates
-- Local short-term increases in noise associated with rehabilitation, demolition and construction
-- Prolonging the life of structures located in areas of high noise exposure
-- Possible destruction of historic structures by demolition
-- Very minor short-term reduction in the available housing stock due to relocations
-- Slight increase in the amount of debris and rubble for disposal in local sanitary landfill operations resulting from structural improvements and demolitions
Public Facilities Projects: Street and Sewers Improvements; Community Center Construction; Handicapped Facilities (Alma, Alviso, Gardner, Mayfair, Northside)
-- Possible disruption of archaeologic sites from subsurface activity
-- Increased long-term energy requirement to serve Alma and Alum Rock Centers
-- Local short-term increases in noise associated with construction of curb ramps
-- Loss of limited habitat due to construction of Alma Neighborhood Center
-- Short-term increases in airborne particulates associated with street and sewer improvements
-- Construction of a public building in an area of high liquefaction potential (Alma Neighborhood Center)
